summary: After the network collapse, Survivor Plaza confronts the immediate question of who has authority to allocate scarce heat, water, food, and medicine.
panelPlan: Wide survivor plaza under improvised lantern clusters with limited supplies visibly separated by type.
A local leader faces several groups asking competing questions at once.
The leader looks at the small resource totals and asks who now has the right to choose.
End on the crowd waiting for an answer no surviving institution has supplied.
directionInline: Open the post-collapse phase with governance reduced to immediate material triage.

dialogueInline.text: I have forty heat packs and eighty-three requests.
Pregnant? Elderly? Anyone on assisted breathing?
You didn't answer me. Who decides?

summary: Aveth answers the authority vacuum by prioritizing heat and water first, taking practical responsibility without claiming a formal title.
panelPlan: Aveth steps into the supply area and starts grouping needs by immediate survival.
Aveth directs water and heat toward the most vulnerable people while others continue arguing legitimacy.
The local leader watches the work begin before consensus exists.
End on people moving because Aveth has made a usable decision.
directionInline: Authority here comes from service and action rather than inherited office.

dialogueInline.text: On the authority of people getting cold while we argue.
Heat and water. Then we count what's left.

summary: In the refugee sector, a displaced family appears differently in three improvised ledgers, turning the argument over restored protocol into an immediate problem of who can actually be found and served.
panelPlan: Establish the cramped refuge rows around a family being reassigned after a pipe burst; handwritten cards, salvaged tablets, and old Cooperative forms all disagree about where they belong.
The Core advocate points to the duplicate household entries as proof that inconsistent rules can make people disappear between systems.
The neighborhood coordinator points to the powerless records office and the broken room that forced the family to move in the first place.
An outer technician working overhead hears the argument while checking a visibly stressed support beam.
directionInline: Give the Core argument real appeal in a frightening environment.

dialogueInline.text: This child is in Row C. Her mother is still listed in Row A.
They moved after the pipe burst.
Then the ledger has to move with them.
The ledger office has no power.
This room has a beam coming down. Argue while you lift.

summary: The neighborhood coordinator defends neighborhood improvisation with a concrete food handoff, while the Core advocate presses the real question of how mistakes are prevented rather than merely traced afterward.
panelPlan: The neighborhood coordinator shows food crates moved directly from a working kitchen to the refuge rows after the central distribution desk failed.
The Core advocate checks one crate's handwritten source tag and asks what would happen if the food had been unsafe.
The neighborhood coordinator can name the kitchen and the people who packed it, but cannot produce a functioning inspection chain.
Above them, the stressed beam gives a sharp metallic complaint and ends the argument mid-sentence.
directionInline: Keep the neighborhood coordinator physically tied to named kitchens, handwritten source tags, and people who can answer for the food; the local model should be visible through practice rather than faction iconography.

dialogueInline.text: That kitchen moved food before anyone could sign it out.
And if somebody had gotten sick?
Knowing who made a mistake is not the same as preventing one.

summary: The political argument stops when the shelter structure begins to fail; all three positions become useful only when converted into a shared physical repair.
panelPlan: The outer technician wedges a temporary support under the dropping beam and calls for bodies and a stronger brace; both advocates move before finishing their argument.
The neighborhood coordinator strips a metal frame while the Core advocate checks which intact support can actually carry the load, each applying a different habit to the same repair.
Final panel: the beam settles onto the improvised brace and the technician looks at both of them, the argument unresolved but the room still standing.
directionInline: Use a physical interruption to puncture abstraction.

dialogueInline.text: I can strip the table frame.
Then help me find something that will.

summary: Ruvian leads a salvage crew into a damaged Outer node where one critical conduit threatens to take the whole system dark.
panelPlan: Wide exposed shard node with open framing, cut panels, and a critical conduit under visible strain.
Ruvian identifies the one failure that would black out the node.
Workers strip salvage from nonessential structure for a brace.
End on Ruvian ordering the conduit held before it buckles.
directionInline: Show the engineering problem clearly enough that the improvisation feels earned.

dialogueInline.text: That conduit goes, we lose the node.
We don't have a brace long enough.
Not if the lights go out.

summary: The outer crew improvises a reinforcement without waiting for central approval, turning emergency habit into an emerging engineering culture.
panelPlan: Workers fit scavenged support around the conduit while sparks fall through the frame.
The outer technician refuses to wait for permission or standardized parts that will not arrive.
Ruvian adapts the brace to the node’s live movement.
End on the crew welding the solution in place.
directionInline: Let the words about grit name a repair culture already visible in the crew’s practiced behavior.

dialogueInline.text: Then stop trying to make it standard.
I can cut the rail and sleeve it.
And when someone asks who approved it?

summary: The patched Outer node holds, giving Ruvian's crew proof that local repair and salvage can sustain infrastructure the old supply system abandoned.
panelPlan: The conduit loads against the new brace as the crew backs away.
Power flickers, then stabilizes across the node.
Workers check pressure and life support rather than celebrating immediately.
End on lights returning through the damaged structure while the improvised brace remains visible.
directionInline: Show the method succeeding materially while keeping the improvised brace and damaged surroundings visible.

dialogueInline.text: I was pleased five minutes ago.
That's why I make you wait.

summary: At Orban, Aveth builds new convoy schedules from eyewitness reports and personal reliability rather than centralized route predictions.
panelPlan: Establish Orban-Tier Transit Port: Aveth covers a wall or table with hand-verified route notes, names, recent sightings, and supply needs.
Port staff compare two possible paths based on who actually traversed them rather than official status.
Supply crates are grouped according to the new trust-route map.
End on Aveth naming trust as the operating requirement.
directionInline: The new system should look practical, provisional, and human-readable.

dialogueInline.text: This route says open. That one says dead.

summary: A port staffer challenges the trust-route model by asking what happens when a trusted person cuts a corner, forcing the new system to acknowledge its own risk.
panelPlan: The staffer points to a route that depends heavily on one unverified report.
Aveth and the staffer examine what redundancy or cross-checking is possible without central data.
The medicine schedule waits on their decision.
End on the open question of how trust remains accountable.
directionInline: Leave the accountability problem genuinely unresolved so trust remains useful but fallible.

dialogueInline.text: What if Jalen cut a corner?
We don't have two for half these routes.
Then mark them yellow and tell the driver exactly why.

summary: Lochran returns to an old BHA safety sigil and argues that recognizable symbols can restore a sense of protection even before institutions are rebuilt.
panelPlan: Establish damaged former BHA space with old markings partly scorched or broken.
Lochran cleans one surviving sigil and traces its familiar shape.
Nearby survivors notice the symbol and understand what it once promised.
End on Lochran insisting that it can mean safety again.
directionInline: The symbol has genuine cultural memory; its power should not feel invented on the spot.

dialogueInline.text: They know what it used to mean.
A door someone can walk through without wondering if the room will kill them.

summary: A field officer warns that repainting the sigil creates a promise of protection they cannot yet guarantee, but begins modifying the mark at Lochran’s request.
panelPlan: The field officer holds paint or marking equipment beneath the damaged old sigil.
They point toward unsafe rooms that the same symbol might falsely authorize.
Lochran maintains that people need a legible sign of order.
End on the officer starting a modified version rather than simply restoring the old mark.
directionInline: Retain the basic geometry of the older BHA safety mark while adding visibly hand-made modifications that narrow what the mark promises.

dialogueInline.text: That's not what the mark says.
You want me to invent a new safety language with a paint brush.
I want people to know where someone has taken responsibility.

summary: Iskari confronts Lochran over using safety symbols without enforceable standards, arguing that a mark without practice becomes a lie.
panelPlan: Iskari finds the newly modified sigil being used around the damaged facility.
She tests or inspects one marked area and finds the underlying safety condition inconsistent.
Facing Lochran, she rejects the idea that the mark itself can substitute for standards.
End on the sigil between them as the object of the dispute.
directionInline: Ground Iskari’s objection in observable inconsistency, not abstract purity.

dialogueInline.text: The room is occupied and monitored.
People cannot parse a standards manual while carrying their children.

summary: Lochran answers that social belief is itself a form of infrastructure and that people need symbols capable of holding communities together.
panelPlan: Lochran points to civilians organizing around marked safe areas despite imperfect conditions.
He argues that shared belief can create coordination before formal systems return.
Iskari sees that he is redefining safety from technical compliance into political trust.
End on Lochran’s claim that belief holds worlds together.
directionInline: Frame Lochran with civilians organizing around the mark and Iskari with the damaged structure it is meant to certify, keeping both arguments physically present.

dialogueInline.text: Look at them. They see the mark and organize around it.
You say that like trust lowers the load on the beam.
No. It gets twelve people out of the rain while someone fixes the beam.

summary: Iskari insists that any shared safety symbol must bind its user to real inspection; Lochran acknowledges the damping-chamber decision without abandoning his belief that institutions must still make promises.
panelPlan: Iskari points from the modified mark to the cracked structure it is supposed to identify, making inspection inseparable from the symbol.
Lochran watches civilians organize around another marked shelter and then looks back at the damaged wall instead of dismissing her concern.
The damping chamber enters the argument without a flashback: Lochran's reaction makes clear that the failed override remains present in every claim he makes about trust.
They part with a narrower disagreement than before: not whether promises matter, but what work must exist before anyone is allowed to make one.
directionInline: Use the environment to keep both philosophies answerable to material conditions.

dialogueInline.text: If we use the symbol, inspection comes with it.
No. The promise and the work arrive together or the promise is false.
I hear the damping chamber every time you say 'false.'
Don't mistake regret for surrender. Someone still has to make promises.

summary: Alone, the field officer finishes a modified safety mark and recognizes that painting it also claims responsibility for whoever trusts it.
panelPlan: Large quiet panel: the field officer stands alone before the modified mark and the damaged doorway, paint still wet and civilians already beginning to use the entrance.
Small final panel on the officer's hand touching the mark after accepting that placing it makes the people behind it their responsibility.
directionInline: Use restraint: one officer, one mark, one imperfect shelter, and the weight of responsibility attached to the final stroke.

dialogueInline.text: If I put this here, I own what happens behind it.

summary: Damiar finds Liora after another move and reveals why she is hiding: several surviving authorities want her account of the damping failure, but they do not agree whether she is a witness, a culprit, or the owner of a text they want to control.
panelPlan: Establish a new, even less comfortable hideout: Liora has packed the treatise for movement rather than settled into a permanent refuge when Damiar arrives with supplies.
Damiar explains that three surviving authorities are looking for her under three different definitions of jurisdiction, and all three have asked about her draft.
Close on Liora taking the paper and filters rather than reacting dramatically; moving again was a deliberate choice to keep both herself and the text outside any one claimant's custody.
directionInline: Make the treatise visibly emerge from the failures, repairs, choices, and records already accumulated around Liora.

dialogueInline.text: Three surviving authorities want you debriefed. Two say inquiry. One says custody.
All three asked whether I had it.
Paper, filters, food. In that order, apparently.

summary: Damiar brings supplies to Liora and admits that he mistook reassurance for duty even when it prevented people from confronting danger.
panelPlan: Damiar arrives with practical supplies rather than official materials.
He notices how directly Liora’s notes connect institutional language to delayed action.
Damiar admits his part without asking for absolution.
End on Liora listening but not interrupting the work.
directionInline: Keep the remorse specific and understated.

dialogueInline.text: I found one of my old statements.
I called the failures temporary for nine days.
You were trying to keep people calm.
I know. That's the part I don't trust anymore.

summary: Liora and Damiar continue working together despite their different histories, converting remorse and technical failure into material future groups will later fight over.
panelPlan: Damiar helps sort records while Liora continues drafting.
They compare an old reassurance statement to the failure timeline it obscured.
Liora leaves contradictory notes visible rather than smoothing them into one doctrine.
End on the growing treatise as unfinished, layered working material.
directionInline: Keep the treatise visibly open and provisional, with contradictions and competing notes still present.

dialogueInline.text: Don't make the lesson 'never reassure anyone.'
That unity was maintenance. We treated it like weather.

summary: Ruvian's crews begin turning improvised repairs into transferable field practice while Nereth, alive and still coordinating from the Broken Node rescue network, circulates failure notes between disconnected engineering crews.
panelPlan: Outer Ring workers compare two independently built versions of the same emergency brace while a narrowband call from Nereth cuts through intermittent static.
Ruvian reports that the second crew changed the brace rather than copying it blindly; Nereth asks for the load, material, and first failure point.
The outer technician notices that relay operators have started filing these reports under the informal label 'Shard repair.'
Ruvian objects to the name only long enough to learn that nobody asked the crews what to call themselves.
Final panel: Nereth tells them to keep the label if it helps the notes travel; another crew receives the same repair file elsewhere.
directionInline: Show the same repair note moving between different crews and being altered with local load, material, and failure information rather than copied as a fixed manual.

dialogueInline.text: Good. Send load, material, and what failed first.
Because nobody asked us what to call it.
Keep the tag. Send the notes.
I hear every bad joke that survives transmission.

summary: Aveth's hand-verified routes acquire an informal name as people begin calling lanes beyond the old centralized map 'verge routes'; Aveth cares less about the label than preserving who actually vouched for each crossing.
panelPlan: At Orban, the rebuilt route board has a blank heading over paths that no longer correspond to official Cooperative lanes.
Port staff report two independent crossings on the south leg and mention the label travelers have started using for routes beyond the old map.
Aveth accepts the practical name but insists that every route still carry the witnesses whose experience made it usable.
End on the board reading VERGE ROUTES with actual crew names and timestamps written immediately beneath it.
directionInline: Show a functioning alternative, not merely a slogan.

dialogueInline.text: The board needs a heading for routes outside the old map.
Who vouched for the south leg?
Mira, then Ko's crew. Two crossings.
People are calling these the verge routes.
Fine. Put the witnesses under the name.

summary: Iskari codifies responsibility as Core, Verge, and Shard practices visibly diverge from the same post-collapse crisis.
panelPlan: Wide montage panel links three simultaneous acts: an outer crew consulting a Shard repair note, an Orban driver checking a named Verge route, and Iskari marking a safety requirement beside a rebuilt facility.
Medium shared-communications panel as Iskari states the minimum documentation and confirmation rules while Ruvian and Aveth challenge how they work when formal institutions are absent.
Final panel holds the three practices side by side without visually merging them: distinct methods growing from the same catastrophe.
directionInline: Show differentiation already underway through distinct practices and visual habits, not suddenly completed factions.

dialogueInline.text: If a brace carries life support, inspection is required. If a route carries medicine, confirmation is required.
And if the inspector never comes?
Then you document what you did and why.

settingText: Cross-cut montage between an Outer Ring repair deck, Orban-Tier Transit Port, and a rebuilt standards workspace: three distinct post-Break practices operating at the same time without sharing one visual language.
